body.statement: For every family \(f=(f_{a,z})\) with \(f_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the constructed law \(P^f\) belongs to \(\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), has residual contribution \(s_{a,z}^{P^f}=f_{a,z}\), and preserves the observed censoring law. On \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\), attainability follows from \(E[(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid a,z,r]=q_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)=f_{a,z}(r)\); on \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\), feasibility forces \(f_{a,z}=0\), and the tie convention keeps the completion legal.
body.justification: This is the attainability step that turns valid inequalities into law sharpness, including zero-capacity contacts.
body.gap: Wang et al. prove endpoint validity in Theorem 5.1 and Appendix D.2 but do not construct one full-data completion attaining an entire shape-coupled curve.
body.consumer: It lets trial analysts interpret every reported curve in the set as arising from an observationally equivalent informative-dropout law.
